# TilePanel

Header: `winui/ui/panels/TilePanel.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panels/TilePanel.hpp`.

A grid of equal cells that children fill in order, each spanning as many rows and columns of cells as it asks for, wrapping to a new line when one is full.

The cell is [item_width()](#item_width) x [item_height()](#item_height), each taken from the first child when unset. Children go first-fit into the free cells, so a small child fills a hole a larger one left behind. A child bigger than the lines is clipped to them. Children that don't fit anywhere are not placed and get an empty rect. The panel asks for the cells it used, plus any alignment offsets. Use it for tile layouts such as a start screen or a photo mosaic. For many items, prefer a virtualizing [TileLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-tilelayoutengine).

Example: 
```cpp
auto grid = std::make_unique<ui::TilePanelControl>();
grid->set_orientation(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
grid->set_item_width(80.0f);
grid->set_item_height(80.0f);
grid->set_maximum_rows_or_columns(4);
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Mail"), 2, 2);   // a 2x2 tile
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Photos"), 1, 2); // one row, two columns
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Maps"));

// Or declaratively:
window.set_content(ui::TilePanel{
    .orientation             = ui::Orientation::Horizontal,
    .item_width              = 80.0f,
    .item_height             = 80.0f,
    .maximum_rows_or_columns = 4,
    .content                 = {
        ui::TilePanelItem{.row_span = 2, .column_span = 2, .content = ui::Button{.text = "Mail"}},
        ui::TilePanelItem{.column_span = 2, .content = ui::Button{.text = "Photos"}},
        ui::TilePanelItem{.content = ui::Button{.text = "Maps"}},
    },
});
```

## `ui::TilePanel`

Equal cells filled in order, children spanning several. Builds a [ui::TilePanelControl](#uitilepanelcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Spec tile(ui::Color c) { return ui::Border{.background = c}; }

window.set_content(ui::TilePanel{
    .orientation             = ui::Orientation::Horizontal,
    .item_width              = 44.0f,
    .item_height             = 44.0f,
    .maximum_rows_or_columns = 3,
    .content                 = {
        ui::TilePanelItem{.content = tile(ui::colors::Black)},
        ui::TilePanelItem{.row_span = 2, .content = tile(ui::colors::White)},
        ui::TilePanelItem{.column_span = 2, .content = tile(ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 120, 215))},
    },
});
```

```cpp
ui::TilePanel{
    .orientation, .item_width, .item_height, .maximum_rows_or_columns,
    .horizontal_children_alignment, .vertical_children_alignment, .background, .style, .margin,
    .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control,
    .content
}
```

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::TilePanelControl](#uitilepanelcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::TilePanelItem`

One child of a [TilePanel](#uitilepanel) with the cell rows and columns it spans. Written inline in the grid's [`.content`](#uitilepanelitem-content); see [ui::TilePanel](#uitilepanel) for an example.

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::TilePanelItem{
    .row_span, .column_span, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uitilepanelitem-row_span"></span>`row_span` | `int` | `1` | Cells covered along the column axis. |
| <span id="uitilepanelitem-column_span"></span>`column_span` | `int` | `1` | Cells covered along the row axis. |
| <span id="uitilepanelitem-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | The placed child. |

## `ui::TilePanelControl`

Derives from `ui::Panel`.

A grid of equal cells that children fill in order, each spanning as many rows and columns of cells as it asks for, wrapping to a new line when one is full.

The cell is [item_width()](#item_width) x [item_height()](#item_height), each taken from the first child when unset. Children go first-fit into the free cells, so a small child fills a hole a larger one left behind. A child bigger than the lines is clipped to them. Children that don't fit anywhere are not placed and get an empty rect. The panel asks for the cells it used, plus any alignment offsets. Use it for tile layouts such as a start screen or a photo mosaic. For many items, prefer a virtualizing [TileLayoutEngine](../controls/item-layouts.md#class-tilelayoutengine).

Example: 
```cpp
auto grid = std::make_unique<ui::TilePanelControl>();
grid->set_orientation(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
grid->set_item_width(80.0f);
grid->set_item_height(80.0f);
grid->set_maximum_rows_or_columns(4);
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Mail"), 2, 2);   // a 2x2 tile
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Photos"), 1, 2); // one row, two columns
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Maps"));

// Or declaratively:
window.set_content(ui::TilePanel{
    .orientation             = ui::Orientation::Horizontal,
    .item_width              = 80.0f,
    .item_height             = 80.0f,
    .maximum_rows_or_columns = 4,
    .content                 = {
        ui::TilePanelItem{.row_span = 2, .column_span = 2, .content = ui::Button{.text = "Mail"}},
        ui::TilePanelItem{.column_span = 2, .content = ui::Button{.text = "Photos"}},
        ui::TilePanelItem{.content = ui::Button{.text = "Maps"}},
    },
});
```

### TilePanelControl

```cpp
TilePanelControl() = default
```

An empty grid: Vertical, cells sized from the first child, no line cap, Leading alignment.

### add

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add(std::unique_ptr<T> child, int row_span = 1, int column_span = 1)
```

Takes ownership of a child spanning [`row_span`](#row_span) x [`column_span`](#column_span) cells (0 counts as 1), appends it after the existing children, and returns a non-owning observer to it.

### add

```cpp
template <SpecLike S>
Element* add(S&& spec, int row_span = 1, int column_span = 1)
```

The declarative overload: builds `spec` (or takes the node a [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec) holds) and adds it as [add()](#add) does a control. Returns the built node as an [Element](../tree/element.md), or nullptr for an empty [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec), which adds nothing; a spec's `.control` field gives a typed observer.

### set_row_span

```cpp
void set_row_span(const Element* child, int span)
```

Changes how many cell rows `child` covers and updates the layout on a change. Ignored when `child` is not one of this grid's children.

### set_column_span

```cpp
void set_column_span(const Element* child, int span)
```

Changes how many cell columns `child` covers.

### row_span

```cpp
int row_span(const Element* child) const
```

The row span given for `child`, or 1 when it is not a child of this grid.

### column_span

```cpp
int column_span(const Element* child) const
```

The column span given for `child`, or 1 when it is not a child of this grid.

### horizontal_children_alignment

```cpp
Alignment horizontal_children_alignment() const
```

Where the block of cells sits horizontally; Leading (Left/Top) by default. In a panel larger than the used cells, Center and Trailing offset the whole block and [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) spreads the lines apart.

### set_horizontal_children_alignment

```cpp

```


### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

True: measuring touches only the panel and its children.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

## class TilePanelItemList

A [TilePanel](#uitilepanel)'s children, built, in the same shape as [CellList](grid.md#uicelllist). Callers write it as a braced list of [`ui::TilePanelItem{...}`](#uitilepanelitem).

### items_

```cpp
std::vector<Placed> items_
```

The placed children, in fill order.

### TilePanelItemList

```cpp
TilePanelItemList() = default
```

An empty list.

### TilePanelItemList

```cpp
template <typename... S>
TilePanelItemList(S&& ... items)
    requires (sizeof...(S) > 0 && (std::same_as<S, TilePanelItem> && ...))
```

Builds every item's content and takes ownership of it.

### TilePanelItemList

```cpp
TilePanelItemList(const TilePanelItemList&) = delete
```

### operator=

```cpp
TilePanelItemList& operator=(const TilePanelItemList&) = delete
```

### TilePanelItemList

```cpp
TilePanelItemList(TilePanelItemList&&) = default
```

### operator=

```cpp
TilePanelItemList& operator=(TilePanelItemList&&) = default
```

### add

```cpp
void add(TilePanelItem item)
```

Builds `item`'s content and appends it, as one more entry of the braced list would.

### struct Placed

One built child with its spans; the node is already owned by the list.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row_span` | `int` |  | [Cell](grid.md#uicell) rows covered. |
| `column_span` | `int` |  | [Cell](grid.md#uicell) columns covered. |
| `node` | `std::unique_ptr<Element>` |  | The built child. |
